.NET 10/C# 14 csharparr: Transmission RPC proxy bridging put.io with *arr services. ASP.NET Core, Serilog, Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience, System.CommandLine, Tomlyn; tests: xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions.

Write concise, idiomatic C#; prefer simplicity, focused solutions. Avoid over-engineering—don't add features, abstractions, or "improvements" beyond what's requested. Don't add features or refactor beyond what's requested. Don't add comments, docstrings, or type annotations to unchanged code. Don't create helpers or abstractions for one-time operations. Don't add error handling for scenarios that can't happen.

Naming: PascalCase public types/members; camelCase locals/parameters; _camelCase private fields; I-prefixed interfaces. Use file-scoped namespaces, records for DTOs/immutable data, pattern matching, nullable references, top-level Program.cs, `[]` for empty collections, `Lock` (not `object`), primary constructors as appropriate. `var` when obvious; focused methods (~50 lines); async all I/O, pass CancellationToken through calls, optional `= default`, Async suffix. Catch `OperationCanceledException` separately; log expected cancellation at Debug, not Error.

Background work: BackgroundService, bounded `Channel<T>` for producer-consumer; track tasks, periodically clean completed tasks. Typed clients for service APIs; named clients for shared config; IHttpClientFactory in background services; per-client timeouts. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` (not deprecated `Polly.Extensions.Http`). Configure exponential-backoff retry with jitter, circuit breaker, appropriate timeouts; retry network errors, timeouts, HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/504.

DI: singleton config; interfaces for services; typed clients with interfaces; factories for dynamic clients. Always register services with their interfaces, not concrete types. Integration-test DI resolution and concurrent resolution.

Use exceptions for exceptional cases, not control flow; domain exceptions. Include HTTP error bodies (truncate at 500 chars). Log BrokenCircuitException at Debug; socket errors Warning without full stack. Continue other operations when a service fails. Structured log templates, never interpolation; levels Debug/Information/Warning/Error/Fatal; suppress framework noise (Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime: Information). Use thread-safe collections/Lock; periodically clean resources.

Tests in `tests/Csharparr.Tests/`: happy/error paths, mock HTTP/external dependencies, FluentAssertions, DI integration; verify controllers/services resolve, see `tests/Integration/`.

Tomlyn; validate at startup with detailed errors, report all errors. Config: username/password basic auth; instance_name 3–10 alphanumeric; instance_folder_id Put.io folder ID; download_directory local path; putio.api_key token; at least one *arr service. Implement Transmission RPC; `[Route("/transmission/rpc")]`; preserve JSON names (`PropertyNamingPolicy = null`). `/health`: simple 200 OK. Docker: multi-stage, non-root, HEALTHCHECK. Platforms: linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-x64, osx-arm64.

Don't use `Polly.Extensions.Http` (deprecated)—use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`. Don't log at Error level for expected conditions (cancellation, circuit breaker). Don't use string interpolation in log messages. Don't register concrete types when interfaces exist.
